style: voices talk and yell, never sing; radio drama, no accompaniment, no tempo, no tune; every outburst is punctuated by a lone string hit and then a hole of quiet; a sforzando violin stab, a Bartok snap pizzicato, col legno wood-on-string crack, a cello falling glissando; siren howl and pounding heartbeat thud as foley between lines, not instruments; cast: hoarse young female medic shrieking until her voice breaks, shrill frightened tenor medic, gravel-voiced older driver bawling; a doddering upper-crust English toff sulking through a car window, met by one sour high harmonic; finishes on an unbroken flatline beep and dead quiet; dry, intimate, cramped, BBC casualty-ward realism
exclude: singing, sung vocals, melody, hook, chorus, rap, beat, drums, groove, bass, pad, sustained strings, piano, choir, cheerful, comedic, upbeat, major key, trailer swell, rhyme, music after the flatline
lyrics:
[Spoken word]
[Siren howling, rain hammering]

[Woman, shrieking, hoarse, voice breaking]
Sixty over thirty! Fucking hurry up, we're gonna lose him!
[Sforzando violin stab. Quiet.]

[Tenor medic, frightened, shrill]
Sats dropping, he's peri-arrest!
[Snap pizzicato. Heartbeat thudding.]

[Driver, gravel voice, bawling]
Two minutes out! Get the fuck out of the way!
[Col legno crack. Brakes. Siren dies.]

[Tenor medic, disbelief]
Why have we stopped?!
[Cello falls away, low]

[Elderly toff, sulking, muffled through glass]
I said raspberry-shaped hors d'oeuvres!
[One sour harmonic]

[Woman, whisper, spent]
Fifty over twen—
[Flatline beep]
[Dead quiet]
[End]
title: PL r3-stab-and-silence
